senses.gloss:
Kabandha Ātharvaṇa is mentioned in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka upaniṣad along with sudhanvan āṅgirasa, as a teacher, but is semi-mythical. His son was vicārin kābandhi.
Foot notes vi. 7, 1. Cf. also Gopatha brāhmaṇa, i. 2, 9. 18; Hillebrandt, Vedische Mythologie, 2, 176, n. 4; Weber, Indian Literature, 149.
Kābandhi (‘descendant of Kabandha’) is the patronymic of Vicārin in the Gopatha brāhmaṇa (i. 2, 9. 18).
